overview.one_line: Built an Android habit-breaking application that interrupts unconscious app usage and encourages mindful digital behavior through behavioral intervention techniques.
overview.summary: OneSec Habit Breaker is an Android application designed to reduce impulsive usage of addictive social media applications such as Instagram, YouTube, Facebook, and Twitter. Instead of blocking apps entirely, the system introduces a deliberate pause between the user's action and app launch, encouraging conscious decision-making. The application monitors selected apps, intercepts launch events, presents a mindfulness screen, and allows users to either continue or cancel the action. The project combines Android development, behavioral design principles, system-level monitoring, and AI-powered usage insights.
overview.elevator_pitch: A digital wellbeing application that helps users break the habit of unconsciously opening social media apps by introducing a short mindfulness interruption before app launch.

problem.statement: Many users open social media applications unconsciously and spend significant amounts of time scrolling without intention. This habitual behavior reduces productivity and contributes to digital distraction.
problem.why_it_matters: Most people do not intentionally spend hours on social media. The problem often starts with an unconscious app launch that gradually turns into extended usage sessions.

motivation.why_i_built_it: I built OneSec primarily for myself after noticing how often I would automatically open social media apps without consciously deciding to do so. I wanted a solution that interrupted the habit loop rather than completely blocking access.
motivation.personal_interest: The project allowed me to combine Android development with behavioral psychology concepts and build a tool that directly solved a problem I personally experienced.

architecture.v1: The first version monitored selected applications and displayed a confirmation screen whenever users attempted to open those apps.
architecture.v2: The application was redesigned with improved UI, enhanced analytics, usage monitoring, and AI-assisted habit insights generated from user interaction data.
architecture.current: Users select apps they consider distracting. The system listens for application launch events and intercepts launches of selected apps. Instead of continuously monitoring the screen, the app relies on Android system events to wake only when required, reducing battery consumption. When a monitored app is launched, a mindfulness screen appears asking whether the user intentionally wants to continue. Users can either proceed to the application or return without opening it. Usage statistics and behavioral patterns are recorded and analyzed to generate personalized insights.
architecture.future: Future versions may include cloud synchronization, user accounts, advanced analytics, personalized habit coaching, cross-device tracking, and Play Store deployment.
